To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the U.S. interest rate is well approximated by a mixture of two autoregressive processes with GARCH errors.
the U.S. 3-month Treasury bill rate is a mixture autoregressive process with GARCH errors.

the mixture autoregressive-GARCH process is a promising model for the U.S. one-month interest rate and that the mixture autogregressive model with GARCH innovations provides a flexible and parsimonious way of modeling the U.S. term structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new class of mixture autoregressions with GARCH errors to the U.S short-term interest rate series.
the modeling of the short-term rate of interest, a central variable in financial economics.
the modeling of the U.S. one-month Treasury Bill rate by a new kind of mixture AR model with GARCH innovations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new model seems to provide a useful alternative to the existing models for short-term interest rates.
the new model is a viable candidate for the U.S. term structure model.
the new mixture autoregressive GARCH model is capable of describing the U.S. interest rate in a way that is consistent with the results in the literature on continuous time models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new mixture autoregressive process is a flexible alternative to the continuous-time diffusion models and the discrete time autoregressive processes that have been the most popular models of the short-term nominal interest rate.
we have developed a new class of mixture autoregressions and applied it to the short-term interest rates.
mixture autoregressive processes provide an alternative to the diffusion approach in the modeling of the short-term U.S. interest rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a parsimonious model of the short-term rate can be constructed that is capable of capturing the most important features of the data and that can be used in the pricing of derivatives.
the new mixture autoregressive process with GARCH errors can be a useful addition to the toolbox of continuous-time diffusion models of interest rates.

the mixture autoregressive models are flexible enough to capture the main empirical features of the short-term rate and that they can be used to generate realizations that have similar properties to the observed data.
